script.base: Dome slog with a small Las Vegas lead. Implied totals are only LV 19.2 and CLE 16.2, so this is not a play-volume game. LV's offense is Brock Bowers (28 targets, 230 yards, 209 air yards in weeks 9-11) plus Ashton Jeanty as a low-efficiency runner (38 carries, 109 yards, 2.87 YPC) and checkdown (18 targets, -54 air). CLE is the dog without Dillon Gabriel, so the recent Gabriel offense (Judkins 48/153, Jeudy 21 targets for 99 yards, Fannin 20/132) is not a clean projection. Base flow: LV protects a one-score lead, Bowers still gets about 6-9 targets because he is the offense, and Quinshon Judkins stays the CLE ball-carrier without stacking 75.5 against a defense allowing 4.00 YPC.
script.flip1: Gabriel's unnamed replacement collapses, LV leads by two scores after halftime and clocks it with Jeanty. Bowers and Jeanty receiving stall late, Judkins' rush line dies as Cleveland chases, and the 16.2 team total never needs a 20-carry game.
script.flip2: Both middle leaks show up (CLE middle 9.14 YPA on 36 throws, LV middle 7.78 on 67) and it plays passier than 35.5. Bowers and Harold Fannin clear; Judkins and Jeanty rush yards stay capped because both teams leave the run. A true shootout is the less likely flip given the total.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both lost. Bowers lost because Las Vegas led by two scores, handed Jeanty the clock, and Cleveland's unnamed linebackers sat on the seam: 4 catches and 38 yards, a replay of the 31-yard game, with the 127-yard outburst exposed as the fluke the 46.5 median was already pricing. Judkins lost because the new quarterback never threatened anyone, Conklin played, and Cleveland ran 24 times at 4.1 a carry with one 18-yard crease, finishing 88 and making the three-game 51-yard average the small sample. That counter-case is real on Bowers' variance and on a hyper-conservative CLE run script, but it is not stronger than six Bowers targets at 8.2 yards per target or than Judkins needing roughly 19 carries at LV's allowed rate just to push 75.5. Keep both and do not size them as if a sim said 70 percent.
slip_story: One low-event dome story, not a shootout stack: Las Vegas still has to throw to Bowers to get to 19 points, and Cleveland's 16.2-point offense does not produce a 75-yard rushing day for Judkins against a 4.00 YPC defense. They win together in the base one-score grind. Do not add a game-total over, a Jeanty rush over, a Tucker over, or any TD. Do not mix in CLE receiver overs while Gabriel is out. Two legs, one market each, no price so no slip is actually placeable.
